reference.title: Barbell Low Split Squat (male)
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Inhale on the way down, exhale on the way up.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s down, short pause, about 1.1 s up

prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg when every rep reaches full depth.

cues.text: Bar on the upper traps just below the bony bump at the base of the neck, hands just outside the shoulders, elbows down, shoulder blades squeezed. Take a long split stance, right foot forward and flat, left heel up on the ball of the foot, feet hip width apart sideways.
Brace and drop the hips straight down, trunk upright under the bar.
Go low: back knee just off the floor, front thigh slightly past parallel, front heel down.
Drive through the front foot to stand back up; breathe out as you rise.
Stand tall in the split stance, re-brace, repeat, then switch legs.

mistakes.fix: Control the last few centimetres and stop just above the floor.

mistakes.mistake: Stance too short for the depth
mistakes.fix: Lengthen the stance until the front heel stays down at the bottom.
Keep the knee over the middle toes.
Keep the chest up and drop straight down.

kinematics.norm: Front knee about over the front foot at the bottom (common guideline); a step about one leg length was suggested as optimal for strength training (Song 2023)
Deeper than the standard split squat: the front thigh passes parallel, about 100-110 degrees (clinical opinion)
Lowers to a few cm off the floor (clinical opinion)
Upright to slightly forward; more lean shifts work to the hip extensors (Farrokhi 2008)
Controlled, about 1-2 s down and 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Low Split Squat (male), video (movement reference only)
Song et al. 2023, effects of step lengths on lower-extremity biomechanics during the split squat (Front Bioeng Biotechnol 11:1277493)
Farrokhi et al. 2008, trunk position influences lead-leg kinematics, kinetics and muscle activity in the forward lunge (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 38:403-409)
Influence of trunk position during three lunge exercises on muscular activation in trained women (PMC8136561)
Mausehund, Skard & Krosshaug 2019, muscle activation in unilateral barbell exercises: implications for strength training and rehabilitation (J Strength Cond Res 33(7S):S85-S94)

cautions: Unrack the bar from a squat rack (J-hooks at about mid-chest height) and re-rack it after the set; set the safeties or use a spotter.
Keep the bar on the muscle of the upper back, never on the neck.
Knee pain at depth: shorten the range.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: A pad under the back knee while learning the depth.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Front-leg knee extensors do most of the work (Mausehund 2019 measured thigh muscle activity in barbell unilateral exercises, the split squat among them).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Front-leg knee extensors do most of the work (Mausehund 2019 measured thigh muscle activity in barbell unilateral exercises, the split squat among them).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Front-leg hip extensor, working harder the deeper the front thigh goes.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Front-leg hip extensor, working harder the deeper the front thigh goes.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and steadies the thigh.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and steadies the thigh.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level and the front knee over the toes on the narrow base.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level and the front knee over the toes on the narrow base.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall and the pelvis level.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk upright; a forward-inclined trunk raises their activity (PMC8136561).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk upright; a forward-inclined trunk raises their activity (PMC8136561).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: The muscle shelf the bar rests on.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: The muscle shelf the bar rests on.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blades together so the upper back forms a tight shelf.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Squeeze the shoulder blades together so the upper back forms a tight shelf.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull the bar down into the back and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull the bar down into the back and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the bar to hold it in place on the back.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the bar to hold it in place on the back.
